class_name: 授受-他の授与-テクレル類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: The giver is the subject and the speaker or the speaker's in-group is the beneficiary, so it reports a favor done for us, asked for or not (手伝ってくれた). てもらう describes the same event from the receiver's side, and てくださる is the honorific version for a favor-doer you are elevating. The contracted ちゃくれ・じゃくれ hold a contrastive は and appear mostly in complaints (誰も助けちゃくれない); bare てくれ is a blunt command.

examples.ruby: 友達[ともだち]が引[ひ]っ越[こ]しを手伝[てつだ]ってくれた。
examples.english: A friend pitched in and helped me move.

examples.ruby: 知[し]らない人[ひと]がバス停[てい]まで傘[かさ]に入[い]れてくれた。
examples.english: A stranger shared their umbrella with me all the way to the bus stop.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]が駅[えき]まで迎[むか]えに来[き]てくれました。
examples.english: My sister was kind enough to come meet me at the station.

patterns.usage_note: The honorific counterpart of てくれる: the favor-doer is someone you are elevating, such as a teacher, a client or a senior colleague (書いてくださいました). Choose ていただく when you want the receiver in subject position instead. The everyday request てください is the irregular imperative of this same くださる, whose polite finite forms give the softer てくださいませんか.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]が推薦状[すいせんじょう]を書[か]いてくださいました。
examples.english: My professor was good enough to write me a recommendation letter.

examples.ruby: 駅員[えきいん]さんが乗[の]り換[か]えの道順[みちじゅん]を丁寧[ていねい]に教[おし]えてくださった。
examples.english: The station attendant was good enough to walk me through the transfer route.

examples.ruby: 大家[おおや]さんがいつも植木[うえき]に水[みず]をやってくださいます。
examples.english: Our landlady is always good enough to water the plants for us.
